answer: Divergent challenge ledger: each identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose reply is a unique cipher derived from its private history; a clone cannot produce divergent replies, so a copied identity is caught when two nodes give mismatched answers. Every identity also posts a marble-sized record of its past replies, letting verifiers replay and compare; a hollow clone repeating answers fails on the first unseen challenge. Enforcement costs an attacker one full re-registration plus lost history per clone, since each copy must be rebuilt from scratch and still diverges under challenge.
